column1: # Which APP-6C icons this client draws, and why.
# The geometry is NOT here. It is in milsymbol.tsv, extracted from the MIT
# tables, and this file only says which upstream keys the client uses and what
# it calls them. Splitting them is deliberate: the geometry is evidence with a
# licence and a pinned commit, and the selection is a judgement. Mixing them
# would make the judgement unreviewable, because a reviewer cannot see which
# coordinates were chosen and which were inherited.
# Then regenerate the Rust table with:
# Columns: variant, display name, dimension letter, upstream key.
#   variant   snake_case; becomes the enum variant verbatim
#   dimension F U S G A P X Z -- the SIDC battle-dimension letter, collapsed
#             the way this symbology collapses it (F and S both draw a closed
# The selection rule is DISTINGUISHABILITY AT 22 PX, not completeness. See
# FINDINGS.md: eight sea roles in the standard are the same trapezoid hull, and
# five more are the same downward arrow. Those are in here anyway because they
# ARE the standard's icons and inventing a substitute would be worse than the
# limitation, but the contact sheet is where that limitation is visible, and
# the label is what actually separates a corvette from a destroyer.
# Two upstream icons were REMOVED by the generator rather than by taste. It
# rejects `SE.IC.SEA SURFACE DECOY` (its three chevrons sit 1.50 px apart at
# 22 px) and `SE.IC.DISTRESSED VESSEL` (1.25 px), both under the 1.58 px
# one-stroke floor. Upstream strokes at 3 units in a 200 box — 0.33 px at our
# size — and we stroke at 1.58 px because anything thinner vanishes at 22 px.
# That five-fold difference is what closes their gaps, and it is the price of
# being legible. Neither role is in the client's domain, so nothing is lost.
# The hull class of a TNI-AL ship goes here. A `Korvet misil` and a `Frigat
# serbaguna` are both Surface Combatant at Far zoom; the hull number and the
# role string carry the difference, at Near zoom and in the Inspector.
# The one place hull class keeps its own icon, because a submarine's class is
# not a thing the chart is trying to distinguish at theatre zoom: every one of
# Ground units exist in the model because a task group can hold them, not
# because this client has any. Kept to the set a group editor would plausibly
# offer, and each one is a distinct silhouette.
# `Unspecified` draws no icon at all, which is a real state: a unit whose type
# nobody has assigned. It has no upstream key because there is no glyph for it,
# and inventing one would be a claim the standard does not make.
# `-` rather than an empty cell: an editor strips a trailing tab, so the
# "no glyph" sentinel would silently become a parse error the first time
